title: Cellular competency reduces selective pressure on structural genes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cellular competency reduces selective pressure on structural genes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the 1D artificial embryogeny model, the genotypic fitness of competent populations rose briefly and then plateaued below that of hardwired populations, with wider variance at higher competency, showing that competency delivers high phenotypic fitness but reduces selective pressure on the structural genes.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 3. Results › 3.2. Developmental Competency Accelerates Evolutionary Search

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, as hypothesized, increasing competency in our simulation enabled excellent performance but reduced selective pressure on the embryo’s structural genes.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Shreesha L, Levin M, “Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2023), doi:10.3390/e25010131; section “3. Results › 3.2. Developmental Competency Accelerates Evolutionary Search”. Scope: In silico 1D artificial embryos evolved with a genetic algorithm

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: All key variables are internal model quantities with explicit definitions. Reimplementation and parameter sweeps can directly resolve the model-specific claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track genotypic and phenotypic fitness distributions through repeated runs at fixed competency levels. Earlier and lower genotypic plateaus plus increasing variance at higher competency confirm the stated masking effect in the model.

fields.label: Evidence against

Results may depend on mutation and selection settings.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The model stores genotypic order separately from post-sorting phenotypic order, and the public experiment already runs the competency sweep. Reanalysis of those runs confirms or refutes the plateau and the variance pattern. No extra biological dataset is required because the claim is about this simulation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: From the same runs, plot genotypic fitness of the best competent individuals against hardwired controls across generations, and compare variance at higher competency. A brief rise then a plateau below the hardwired trajectory, with wider variance at higher competency, would confirm the claim; genotypic fitness tracking phenotypic fitness would refute reduced selective pressure.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Plateau height depends on how many bubble-sort steps the competency parameter allows.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In a re-run of the Shreesha & Levin (2023) Experiment 1 model (fixed competency 20/100/400 vs hardwired, 100 repeats x 250 generations), the best genotypic fitness of each competent population stops rising and stays below the hardwired population's, its spread across repeats grows with competency, while phenotypic fitness stays high.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered, with 'best genotypic fitness' = the maximum genotypic (pre-development) fitness in the population each generation, as in the authors' code: (A) at generation 250 each competent population's mean best genotypic fitness is below hardwired, one-sided Welch t-test p < 0.001; (B) plateau: for each competency level, |mean of the mean curve over generations 226-250 minus mean over generations 126-150| < 0.03; (C) the across-repeat standard deviation of best genotypic fitness, averaged over generations 51-250, is strictly ordered competency 20 < 100 < 400; (D) mean best phenotypic fitness at generation 250 >= 0.95 for every competency level. All four -> supports.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: refutes if any competent level's mean best genotypic fitness at generation 250 is >= hardwired, or the generation-51-250 SD at competency 400 is below that at competency 20, or any competent level's genotypic mean curve still rises by more than 0.1 between the 126-150 and 226-250 windows. Any other failure of (A)-(D) -> mixed.
